title: Buying the Verdict
authors: Lauren H. Cohen; Umit G. Gurun
eligible_reason: Firm x DMA x year panel (Audit Analytics litigation, Kantar ad spending), 1995-2013. Treatment defendant (copied into sued_all) = 1 if the firm is a defendant in a trial in a court mapped to that DMA in year t; it switches on at firm-DMA-specific years (many first-suit cohorts 1995-2012) and most firm-DMA pairs are never sued. Table 3 (baseline) columns 1 and 2 are plain TWFE with no controls: reghdfe initiate sued_all, absorb(permnoxdma year) and reghdfe adspend_t1 sued_all if adspend_t0>0, absorb(permnoxdma year), clustered by permno x year. Columns 3-4 add adspend_t0 (the lagged outcome, since the outcome is adspend_t1) and total_dma_ad (time-varying); all Table 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 columns and Exhibit 1 also include adspend_t0; Table 5 adds total_dma_ad (time-varying control only). The treatment is a transient lawsuit-year indicator that switches off and on again (269 post-first-suit rows with treatment 0 vs 193 treated rows in the shipped extract), so the Hull fn. 6 switch-off rule (drop post-adoption rows with treatment 0) leaves essentially first-suit-year effects. ELIGIBLE with a data flag: the package ships a 20-firm extract (7,236 rows) of the estimation file, not the full sample (published N = 485,704 for Table 3 col 1).
design_notes: Stata reghdfe, code in replication_package_MS-FIN-21-01549/bv_main.do (single do-file; log_of_results.smcl holds the authors' full-sample output). Unit = permnoxdma (firm x DMA), time = year, FE permnoxdma + year, cluster permnoxyear. adspend_t1 = log ad expense in t+1 (variable dictionary), adspend_t0 = log ad expense in t; initiate = 1 if the firm advertises in the DMA for the first time (in the extract initiate == 1 exactly when adspend_t0 == 0; 127 of 193 defendant rows have initiate == 1, so many firm-DMA cells enter the panel through the lawsuit). Panel is highly unbalanced (153 of 823 firm-DMA cells observed once; 315 internal year gaps) and 48 of 92 treated cells are treated in their first observed year (always-treated, dropped by CSA). Published Table 3 (log): col 1 initiate 0.2539 (0.0062), N 485,704; col 2 adspend_t1 0.1696 (0.0623), N 478,840; col 3 (with adspend_t0) 0.2358 (0.0539) is the abstract's 23% (t = 4.37). Table 4 col 2 recodes treatment to exclude first-time suits (x_sued_f) and Table 6 splits treatment by litigation type (extra treatment regressors). Table 10 regresses verdict outcomes (defwon) on ad spending (not DiD). Appendix II uses firm x year and DMA FE; Appendix III a difference specification.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: First-suit years 1995-2012 in the shipped 20-firm extract (14 cohorts with an untreated pre-period in the extract); full sample not shipped.

specs.outcome: initiate (=1 if the firm advertises in the DMA for the first time; next-year entry into DMA advertising)
specs.treatment_definition: defendant = 1 if the firm is a defendant in a trial in a court mapped to DMA d in year t
specs.sample_condition: e(sample) of the same regression (keep if e(sample)); singletons dropped by reghdfe
specs.notes: Treatment switches off and on (lawsuit-year indicator); drop post-first-suit rows with defendant == 0 (Hull fn. 6). Shipped data are a 20-firm extract, so the published coefficient cannot be reproduced.

specs.outcome: adspend_t1 (log total ad expense of the firm in the DMA in year t+1)
specs.treatment_definition: defendant = 1 if the firm is a defendant in a trial in a court mapped to DMA d in year t
specs.sample_condition: adspend_t0 > 0 (firm advertised in the DMA in year t); estimated on the Table 3 col 1 e(sample)
specs.notes: Sample condition is on a time-varying (concurrent) spending variable; recorded as published. Switch-off rule as in T3c1.

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: adspend_t0 is the lagged outcome (outcome adspend_t1); col 4 also adds total_dma_ad
lagged outcome adspend_t0 in every column; Tables 6-9 also add extra treatment regressors or subgroup-by-treatment interactions
time-varying control total_dma_ad only (5c-type column, but the paper is already eligible via Table 3)
verdict outcome regressed on ad spending; not a DiD

data_files_note: combined_lit_ad.dta ships 7,236 rows (20 permnos, 101 DMAs, 823 firm-DMA cells, 1995-2013); the authors' log shows 485,704 observations and 62,485 firm-DMA cells for Table 3 col 1. README lists licensed sources (Audit Analytics, Kantar Media Stradegy, Nielsen, CRSP/Compustat, RavenPack) and says several linking files are provided only to subscribers; it does not say that the shipped files are extracts or how the 20 firms were chosen.
